chunks: Surely for him who comes before his Lord a sinner shall be Hell, where he will neither die nor live.

key_terms.جَهَنَّمَ: Hell, the place of punishment in the afterlife
key_terms.لَا يَمُوتُ: He will not die, implying the end of suffering does not come
key_terms.مُجْرِمًا: Sinner or criminal, one who commits sins
key_terms.وَلَا يَحْيَى: And he will not live, implying no ease or comfort in the state of torment

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the inhabitants of Hell will neither die nor live?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (20:74) is often linked with 20:75 to contrast the fate of the arrogant sinner with the humble believer, emphasizing that 'not dying' refers to the cessation of death's relief while 'not living' denotes the absence of ease. This perpetual state underscores the justice of Allah, where the punishment fits the magnitude of the sin, serving as a warning against those who meet their Lord with unrepentant arrogance.
